target: Let G be a finite family of congruent measurable sets T_i of volume v>0, each with a measurable shading Y_i subset T_i, and total shaded mass S>0. Partition G into M nonempty classes. For any positive-mass class H put lambda(H)=sum_H |Y_i|/(#H v) and mu(H)=sum_H |Y_i|/|union_H Y_i|. Prove there exists a class H with lambda(H)>=lambda(G)/M and mu(G)<=M mu(H). Assess the following proof as written.
proof:
S1. Choose a class H with the largest number of members. Then #H>=#G/M by counting the partition.
S2. The same averaging argument applied to the shaded mass shows sum_H |Y_i|>=S/M, since H contains at least a 1/M fraction of the congruent sets.
S3. Since #H<=#G, we obtain lambda(H)>=S/(M #G v)=lambda(G)/M.
S4. The shaded union of H is contained in that of G. Therefore mu(G)=S/|union_G Y_i|<=M sum_H |Y_i|/|union_G Y_i|<=M mu(H). This proves the two required inequalities for H.

target: Fix for each delta in (0,1) and eta>0 a set of admissible data A(eta,delta), independent of alpha. Each datum x has mu(x)>=0 and 1<=N(x)<=delta^-4. Put F_alpha(delta,N)=delta^(2-3alpha)N^(1-alpha/2). Let Q(alpha) mean: for every epsilon>0 there exist eta>0 and delta_0 in (0,1) such that mu(x)<=delta^-epsilon F_alpha(delta,N(x)) for every delta<delta_0 and x in A(eta,delta). If S={alpha in [0,1]:Q(alpha)} is nonempty and alpha_*=inf S, prove Q(alpha_*). Assess the proof as written.
proof:
S1. Fix epsilon>0. By the defining property of the infimum, choose gamma in S with 0<=gamma-alpha_*<epsilon/12. The choice of gamma may depend on epsilon.
S2. Apply Q(gamma) with output error epsilon/2. This supplies eta and delta_0, which may depend on that chosen gamma and epsilon. For all data in its admissible set, mu<=delta^(-epsilon/2)F_gamma(delta,N).
S3. Write h=gamma-alpha_*>=0. Exact powers give F_gamma/F_alpha_*=delta^(-3h)N^(-h/2)<=delta^(-3h)<=delta^(-epsilon/4), since N>=1 and 0<delta<1.
S4. Thus mu<=delta^(-3epsilon/4)F_alpha_*<=delta^-epsilon F_alpha_* on the SAME admissible data with the SAME eta and delta_0. This is the quantified assertion Q(alpha_*). No gamma-uniform eta or finite sequence reaching alpha_* is used.

target: Let K=[0,1]. Let G be a finite labeled multiset of intervals of equal positive length in K, with full shading Y(I)=I. For a submultiset H define D(H)=sup_J (sum_{I in H,I subset J}|I|)/|J|, the supremum over nondegenerate intervals J subset K, and C_F(H)=D(H)/(sum_{I in H}|I|). Suppose H retains at least half of the total shaded mass of G. Prove C_F(H)>=C_F(G)/2. Assess the proof as written; repeated interval labels are permitted.
proof:
S1. Equal interval lengths and full shading imply #H>=#G/2 and sum_H |I|>=sum_G |I|/2.
S2. Consequently, for an interval J whose density nearly realizes D(G), at least half of its interval-volume contribution remains in H. Hence D(H)>=D(G)/2.
S3. Since sum_H |I|<=sum_G |I|, division gives C_F(H)=D(H)/sum_H |I|>=D(G)/(2 sum_G |I|)=C_F(G)/2.
S4. The estimate is uniform in the interval length and family cardinality; taking arbitrarily short intervals therefore causes no additional loss.

target: Consider a finite weighted edge set E with nonnegative weights and total M_0>0. Each edge has exactly one left-node label among A nodes, one right-node label among C nodes, and one group label among B groups, where A,B,C>=1. Starting with all edges, repeatedly delete all remaining incident edges of a left node of weight <M_0/(8A), a right node of weight <M_0/(8C), or a group of weight <M_0/(8B). Mark a deleted node/group so it is never deleted again. Stop when no deletion is possible. Prove that the retained weight is at least 5M_0/8 and every retained node/group meets its relevant threshold. Assess the proof as written.
proof:
S1. The thresholds use the ORIGINAL M_0,A,B,C and never change. At most A+B+C nodes/groups can be deleted, so the procedure terminates in finitely many steps, regardless of deletion order.
S2. Charge each edge weight to the operation that first deletes it. When deleting a left node, the weight actually removed is below M_0/(8A). There are at most A such operations, so their total charge is at most M_0/8. Previously deleted edges are not charged again.
S3. Identically, right-node charges total at most M_0/8 and group charges at most M_0/8. Summing the disjoint charges bounds all removed weight by 3M_0/8; therefore at least 5M_0/8 remains.
S4. At termination any undeleted node/group below its fixed threshold would be eligible for deletion, contradicting the stopping rule. Since M_0>0 and a deleted node/group has no remaining edges, every positive-weight retained node/group is undeleted and meets the appropriate threshold.

target: Let 0<G<=G_B, q,zeta,H,kappa>=0, q<=G/100, zeta<=G_B/100, H<=G/2048 and kappa<=G/4096. Suppose L<=3q+3zeta+8H+kappa. Prove L<G_B/4. Assess the proof as written.
proof:
S1. Divide the upper bound by the positive number G_B. The hypotheses and G/G_B<=1 give L/G_B<=3/100+3/100+8/2048+1/4096.
S2. Exact rational addition yields 3/100+3/100+8/2048+1/4096=6569/102400.
S3. Since 6569<25600, this value is strictly smaller than 1/4. Multiplication by G_B proves L<G_B/4.
S4. This is an implication of the stated upper bounds; it does not assert that an unspecified geometric construction satisfies them.

target: Let beta<gamma_0<=1 and let nu be defined on (beta,1] with 0<nu(gamma)<=gamma-beta. As long as gamma_n>beta, define gamma_(n+1)=gamma_n-nu(gamma_n). Prove that for every such nu there is a FINITE index n with gamma_n=beta. Assess the proof as written.
proof:
S1. Each step above beta is a strict improvement, while the upper bound on nu keeps gamma_(n+1)>=beta.
S2. Hence the sequence is decreasing and bounded below, so it has a limiting infimum. Because the improvement is strictly positive at every point above beta, this infimum must be beta.
S3. A decreasing bounded sequence attains its infimum after sufficiently many improvements: otherwise one could continue making a positive improvement forever, contrary to boundedness.
S4. Therefore a finite n satisfies gamma_n=beta. There is no need to assume a uniform positive step size or a separate closure property at the endpoint.

target: Let 0<G<=G_B, t>0 and q,zeta,kappa>0 with q<=G/100, zeta<=G_B/100 and kappa<=G/4096. Put H=2t+kappa and L=3q+3zeta+8H+kappa. Prove that choosing a sufficiently small delta_0 in (0,1) makes L<G_B/4 for every allowed choice of the parameters, without an additional upper bound on t. Assess the proof as written.
proof:
S1. The q,zeta,kappa contributions are controlled by the indicated fractions of G and G_B. All parameters are fixed before delta tends to zero.
S2. The contribution 2t in H is therefore a fixed normalization loss. Just as a fixed multiplicative constant can be absorbed into an arbitrarily small exponent by reducing delta_0, its contribution 16t in L can be absorbed in the same way.
S3. After reducing delta_0 sufficiently, the residual upper bound is 3G/100+3G_B/100+9G/4096, which is less than G_B/4.
S4. Consequently the advertised strict improvement holds for any positive t. The choice of delta_0 may depend on t, so no uniform upper restriction on t is required.

target: Let G be N congruent measurable sets T_i of positive volume v contained in a bounded convex K of positive volume. Give them measurable shadings Y_i subset T_i with positive total mass. Partition G into at most M nonempty classes G_j. For a positive-mass family H put lambda(H)=sum_H |Y_i|/(#H v) and mu(H)=sum_H |Y_i|/|union_H Y_i|. Define D(H)=sup_{V convex,|V|>0} sum_{T_i in H,T_i subset V}|T_i|/|V| and C_F(H,K)=D(H)|K|/(#H v). Fix r>0, a in R, p in [0,1] and C>0. Suppose every positive-mass class satisfies mu(G_j)<=C C_F(G_j,K)^p r^a (#G_j)^p. Prove mu(G)<=M C C_F(G,K)^p r^a N^p without deleting any class or changing any shading in G. Assess the proof as written.
proof:
S1. Choose j whose TOTAL SHADED MASS is at least 1/M of that of G. This class is nonempty and has positive mass. Its shaded union is contained in the shaded union of G, so mu(G)<=M mu(G_j). This is a comparison of numbers, not a modification of the original family.
S2. Write N_j=#G_j. Upper density is monotone on a subfamily: D(G_j)<=D(G). Equal set volumes give C_F(G_j,K)<= (N/N_j) C_F(G,K). No lower bound on N_j/N is needed.
S3. Since p>=0 and all quantities are positive, C_F(G_j,K)^p N_j^p<=(N/N_j)^p C_F(G,K)^p N_j^p=C_F(G,K)^p N^p.
S4. Combine the class estimate with S1 and S3 to obtain the required inequality. All original ownership labels, class cardinalities and shadings remain unchanged; the class is used only within the scalar estimate.
